desc:
You must ride n trains in order. Train i covers dist[i] kilometres. All trains travel at the same constant integer speed s km/h (the one number you choose). A train can only depart at the start of a whole hour, so after finishing train i you wait until the next whole hour before boarding train i + 1. The last train needs no waiting afterwards.

You must reach the destination within hour / 100 hours; the allowed time is given in hundredths of an hour so that everything stays an integer (for example hour = 275 means 2.75 hours).

Return the smallest positive integer speed that makes it on time, or -1 if no speed works. Whenever an answer exists, it is at most 107.

Example: dist = [1, 3, 2], hour = 270. At speed 3 the trips last 1 h, 1 h and 2/3 h, giving 2 + 0.67 = 2.67 ≤ 2.70. At speed 2 they take 1 h, 2 h and 1 h, which is 4 h. The answer is 3.
constraints: If an answer exists it is at most 10<sup>7</sup>
hints: Write the total travel time as a function of the speed s: every train except the last takes ceil(dist[i] / s) hours, the last takes exactly dist[last] / s hours.
A faster speed never makes the total slower. Also, you need at least n - 1 full hours for the first n - 1 trains, so if hour ≤ 100 * (n - 1) the answer is -1.

Binary search the speed in [1, 10^7]. To avoid floating point, test (T * s + dist[last]) * 100 ≤ hour * s where T is the sum of the rounded-up hours of the first n - 1 trains. If even 10^7 fails, return -1.
editorial: For a speed s, the total time is T(s) + dist[n-1] / s where T(s) = sum(ceil(dist[i] / s)) over the first n - 1 trains. Both parts are non-increasing in s, so the set of speeds that arrive on time is a suffix of the positive integers: binary search for the first one.

Avoid floats: multiply the inequality T + d / s ≤ hour / 100 by 100 * s to get 100 * (T * s + d) ≤ hour * s, which uses integers only. The upper limit 107 is enough because at that speed every train takes one hour (or the last takes at most 0.01 h) so any larger speed cannot help; if the check fails there, no speed works and the answer is -1. Complexity is O(n log 107) time and O(1) space.
